clippings.speaker: Cary Grant
clippings.quote: I have only happy ones. They’re all vivid because they’re all interesting. It was a great joy to work with Hitch. He was an extraordinary man. I deplore these idiotic books written about him when the man can’t defend himself.
clippings.title: New Again: Cary Grant
clippings.context: Asked by Kent Schuelke for his memories of working with Hitchcock, four months before Grant's death; republished online in 2013.

clippings.speaker: Cary Grant
clippings.quote: A film’s a film. As Hitch would say when someone would get all upset on the set, “Come on, fellas, relax—it’s only a movie.”
clippings.title: New Again: Cary Grant
clippings.context: Grant, asked whether scholars over-analyze films made for entertainment, recalls Hitchcock's on-set refrain.

clippings.speaker: Cary Grant
clippings.quote: When we were making Notorious, Ingrid could do no wrong as far as Alfred Hitchcock was concerned. He simply adored her. … I always went to work whistling when I was working on a Hitchcock film because nothing ever went wrong. Hitch was so incredibly well prepared.
clippings.title: A Few Words with Cary Grant
clippings.context: Phone interview with Philip Wuntch ahead of Grant's Dallas 'Conversation' appearance; fan-site reprint of the newspaper article.

clippings.speaker: Alfred Hitchcock
clippings.quote: In the case of Suspicion, one of the early films you mention with Cary Grant, he should never have been in the picture in the first place. You run into this problem. You cast a man who is suspected of murder and then you have to compromise.
clippings.title: Alfred Hitchcock at the National Film Theatre
clippings.context: Interviewed by Bryan Forbes at London's National Film Theatre, broadcast by BBC One; transcript excerpt reproduced by Cinephilia & Beyond.

clippings.speaker: Alfred Hitchcock
clippings.quote: The scene I wanted, but it was never shot, was for Cary Grant to bring her a glass of milk that’s been poisoned … Fade out and fade in on one short shot: Cary Grant, whistling cheerfully, walks over to the mailbox and pops the letter in. That would have been a great twist.
clippings.title: ‘Suspicion’: Proof that a True Artist Can Create Great Things Even Under the Crippling Harness of a Profit-Driven Studio
clippings.context: From Hitchcock's 1962 interviews with François Truffaut, describing the ending he wanted for Grant's character; book excerpt reproduced online.

clippings.speaker: Alfred Hitchcock
clippings.quote: Anyway, Cary Grant came up to me and said, ‘It’s a terrible script. We’ve already done a third of the picture, and I still can’t make head or tail of it.’ …Without realizing it he was using a line of his own dialogue.
clippings.title: 4K UHD Blu-ray Review: North by Northwest
clippings.context: Hitchcock to Truffaut on Grant's confusion during North by Northwest, which suited his bewildered character; excerpt quoted in a blog review.

notes: Famous 'only actor I ever loved' line has no traceable original, skipped; hitchcock.zone (AFI 1979 transcript) unreachable and Greg Joseph Medium interview blocked.
